title: A bill is introduced
caption: A bill can be brought by the Executive or by a member of either chamber. It may start in the Senate or in the House of Representatives.

check.question: In which chamber may a bill begin?
check.explain: A bill may originate in either the Senate or the House of Representatives.

title: First Reading
caption: The bill's title is read to the chamber. There is no debate at this stage — it simply puts the bill formally before the House.

title: Second Reading
caption: Members debate the general principles of the bill — what it is for, not yet its exact wording. A bill that loses this debate goes no further.

title: Committee Stage
caption: A committee examines the bill clause by clause and can hold a public hearing, where citizens and experts give evidence. Most of the real work happens here.

title: Report Stage
caption: The committee reports back and the chamber works through its recommendations, settling the wording the bill will carry forward.

title: Third Reading
caption: The chamber takes its final vote. If the bill passes, it has cleared this chamber — but it is still not law.

title: The other chamber
caption: The bill is transmitted to the other chamber, which puts it through the same stages. Both the Senate and the House of Representatives must pass it.

check.question: One chamber has passed the bill. What has to happen before it can go to the President?
options: The other chamber must pass it, and the two must agree on any amendment
A joint sitting of both chambers must vote on it
check.explain: A bill passed by the chamber it started in is sent to the other. It is presented to the President only when that chamber has passed it too and the two have agreed on any amendment.

title: Harmonisation
caption: If the two chambers pass different versions, a conference committee drawn from both produces a single text — and each chamber must then adopt it.

title: Presidential assent
caption: The agreed copy goes to the President, who has thirty days to assent to the bill or to withhold assent.

check.question: How long does the President have to assent or withhold assent?
check.explain: Once a bill is presented, the President has thirty days to signify either assent or the withholding of it.

title: It becomes law
caption: With assent, the bill becomes an Act of the National Assembly. If assent is withheld, it can still become law — but only if each chamber passes it again by a two-thirds majority.

check.question: Assent is withheld. What does it take to make the bill law anyway?
options: A simple majority in each chamber
A two-thirds majority in each chamber
check.explain: If the bill is passed again by each chamber by a two-thirds majority, it becomes law and the President's assent is not required.
